newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Comalco sees strong long term outlook.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Comalco sees strong long term outlook.

text.p: Aluminium producer Comalco Ltd said on Monday the longer term outlook for the company was strong, despite a sharply lower profit for the year to June 30, 1996.

"The longer term outlook for Comalco is strong. We have sold most of our downstream operations and are concentrating on upstream growth opportunities," Comalco chief executive Terry Palmer said in a statement.
"These include expansions and upgrades of the existing smelters and the feasibility study on a new alumina refinery," Palmer said.
"In addition we remain alert to other opportunities in smelting and refining," he said.

Comalco's first half net profit on a joint venture basis was A$50.6 million, down from A$96.6 million in the previous comparable half year. It posted a three cent interim dividend, down from 12 cents in 1995. Comalco's pre-abnormal net on a joint venture basis was A$43.9 million. Analysts had expected a pre-abnormals net of between A$55 million and A$67 million.
Comalco's Palmer said the result was achieved in difficult market conditions. Comalco is 67 percent owned by RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd.
"Lower primary aluminium prices, movements in the exchange rate, softer alumina markets and weaker alumina spot prices affected profit," he said.
Comalco's smelting division was severely affected by the declining London Metal Exchange (LME) price for aluminium.
Palmer said excellent progress had been made on the expansion of the Boyne Island smelter in Queensland and on the upgrade of the Tiwai Point smelter in New Zealand.
"The Boyne Island smelter is ahead of its construction schedule and budget and is expected to begin producing its first metal in mid-1997," Palmer said.
He said Comalco was progressively restarting idled capacity at the Bell Bay smelter in Tasmania and expected it to produce 119,000 tonnes of aluminium this year.
"In 1997, the smelter will be capable of producing almost 140,000 tonnes per year," he said.
Comalco said the outlook for world aluminium supply and demand was expected to come into balance over the second half of this year and into 1997.
It said aluminium exports from the CIS were expected to decline due to internal economic growth while Western world demand should continue to grow modestly.
Continued restraint by the major producers in bringing on idle capacity should keep supply under control.
"There are no major capacity expansions scheduled to come on line until after mid-1997," it said.
Comalco share closed eight cents lower at A$7.48 on Friday.
